title: When Validators Don’t Trigger: A Paired Evaluation of Generate→Validate→Repair for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired experiment to evaluate whether a validator‑guided repair pipeline (generate→validate→repair) reduces high‑risk semantic misconfigurations compared with single‑shot LLM generation in intent→vendor‑configuration tasks for NetOps. Using a preregistered paired design (N=600 task pairs), a single shared initial candidate per pair (generation_semantics=shared_initial_candidate), and gpt-5-mini as the generative model, each pair compared: (a) baseline: the shared initial candidate accepted as final, versus (b) guarded: the same shared initial candidate subject to deterministic validator checks and at most one automated repair. Deterministic_netops_validator_v5 judged final semantic validity. All 600 pairs produced validator‑passing configurations in both conditions (baseline success rate = 100%, guarded = 100%); the paired absolute difference = 0.0 (95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). Confirmatory hypothesis H1 (tool‑augmented pipeline reduces high‑risk failures) was not supported because no validator failures occurred and thus no repairs executed. We report preregistration details, full execution accounting, and discuss design, construct validity of the validator, implications of the shared_initial_candidate execution semantics, and recommendations for future NetOps safety evaluations.

sections.introduction: Intent‑driven NetOps seeks to map high‑level operator intents into low‑level vendor configurations. Prior work documents promising LLM‑based intent translation prototypes and improvements from tool augmentation (validators, calculators, or code interpreters), but large open questions remain about operational reliability under adversarial or out‑of‑distribution intents and about evaluation methodology [1][2][3]. We preregistered a focused confirmatory study asking: Under a controlled paired design, does a validator‑guided repair pipeline reduce high‑risk semantic misconfigurations relative to single‑shot LLM generation? Our contributions: (1) a preregistered paired experiment executed on 600 intent→configuration pairs; (2) complete execution artifacts and deterministic validator traces; (3) a null but informative outcome that exposes an important experimental-design interaction (shared_initial_candidate semantics and validator sensitivity) with operational implications.
sections.related_work: LLM approaches for intent→configuration and intent translation have been proposed and prototyped with encouraging task‑level results but typically in testbeds or limited corpora [1][4]. Empirical studies across domains show that tool‑augmented LLMs (RAG, task calculators, validator tools) often reduce classes of errors compared with baseline LLM outputs [5][6]. Hallucination and semantic/functional errors in model outputs are well documented and motivate generate→validate→repair pipelines and constrained/neurosymbolic decoding techniques that enforce syntax or richer semantics at generation time [7][8][9]. Our study tests one operational instantiation of validator‑guided repair under tightly controlled paired semantics.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: We preregistered study autocand-2026-01-prereg-v1 before observing outcomes. The design was paired and confirmatory: 600 deterministic task pairs selected by the adapter contract (planned_episode_count=1200; completed_episode_count=1200). Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in high‑risk semantic failure proportions (guarded minus baseline), computed by the paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. Execution adapter and model: adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; declared generative model gpt-5-mini. Generation semantics: shared_initial_candidate — exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was reused by both baseline and guarded conditions. Temperature: the archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset. Null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling; we recorded and archived all runtime sampling fields. Tasks and validator: Tasks were synthetic intent→configuration problems produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with explicit required sequences and workflow constraints; deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performed a machine‑deterministic intent‑constraint validation (full_intent_constraint_validation) producing binary pass/fail outcomes and traces. Confirmatory policy allowed at most one automated repair call per guarded episode, invoked only if the validator failed. Inclusion/exclusion: only redistributable items with public provenance were included in the confirmatory sample per the preregistered contamination plan. Analysis plan: McNemar‑style paired test (exact) and paired bootstrap CIs; failed_call_treatment = complete_pair_primary.
sections.results: Execution and primary outcome: Execution_manifest shows completed_episode_count = 1200, model_calls_used = 600 (one shared initial generation per pair), and failed_episode_count = 0. Deterministic validator outcomes: baseline success_count = 600/600 (100%); guarded success_count = 600/600 (100%). Contingency: n11 = 600, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. No guarded repair calls were executed because no validator failures occurred. Secondary preregistered analyses (vendor strata, repair success rates, failure‑mode breakdowns) are not informative because no failures were observed; all such summaries are provided in the archived analysis artifacts.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: The preregistered guarded pipeline provided no observable benefit in this execution because the deterministic validator accepted the shared initial candidate in every pair, leaving no opportunity for automated repair. This null result is informative: it shows that, under (a) the chosen task bank, (b) validator sensitivity, and (c) shared_initial_candidate semantics, the guarded pipeline cannot improve outcomes if the validator does not flag any initial outputs. Design implications: (1) shared_initial_candidate semantics must be understood: under this contract baseline and guarded begin from the same initial model draw, so any difference can only arise from validator‑triggered repair; claims about guarded improving a separate first‑pass generation are incorrect under these semantics. (2) Validator construct validity is critical: a permissive validator or insufficiently challenging tasks will produce ceiling performance that masks pipeline differences. (3) Temperature=null/unset in archived configuration does not imply deterministic model sampling; future runs should record explicit sampling parameters or use multiple independent initial draws per condition when the goal is to measure generation‑level differences. Limitations and recommended next steps: evaluate on harder or adversarially adversarialized tasks, use an independent per‑condition generation arm (no shared_initial_candidate) to measure generation differences, or employ stricter validators (or multiple validators) that detect subtler semantic failures. Broadly, empirical conclusions about the value of tool‑augmentation require both challenging task banks and validators with demonstrated sensitivity to operationally relevant semantic failures.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered paired experiment (N=600 pairs) comparing single‑shot LLM generation and a validator‑guided repair pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Both conditions passed the deterministic validator in all pairs (100% baseline and guarded success), yielding an estimated paired difference of 0.0 (95% CI [0.0,0.0], p=1.0). The absence of validator failures prevented any repair interventions and therefore precluded evidence that the guarded pipeline reduces high‑risk semantic failures in this specific execution. The result emphasizes (1) the experimental dependence on execution semantics (shared initial draws), (2) the centrality of validator construct validity, and (3) the need for more adversarial and diverse NetOps task banks and independent‑generation designs to measure the true operational benefit of generate→validate→repair architectures.

disclosure_statement: Models and tools: All generative calls used the declared model gpt-5-mini via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. The deterministic validator was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration and autonomy: The experiment was preregistered as autocand-2026-01-prereg-v1 prior to observing outcomes and executed autonomously under that plan. Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family and initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the lock the AI system autonomously selected the final research question, executed the preregistered experiment, performed analyses, and drafted the manuscript. No manual human editing of technical content or results occurred after the autonomy lock. Master prompt reference: initial_master_prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Generation semantics and sampling: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (the same single sampled initial generation per pair was reused by baseline and guarded). The archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is explicitly not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was reused by baseline and guarded; only validator‑triggered repair calls could create paired outcome differences. Preregistered limits and artifacts: the preregistered confirmatory sample used only redistributable public items per the contamination plan; execution manifest, raw outputs, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived. Deviations: none of the preregistered confirmatory design elements (shared_initial_candidate semantics, one initial generation per pair, permitted repair policy) were changed after seeing outcomes.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate execution semantics: baseline and guarded used the identical initial model draw per pair; thus guarded could differ only if the validator rejected the initial candidate and repair executed. The design therefore measures validator/repair effectiveness, not independent generation differences.

Validator construct validity: a permissive or incomplete validator can produce ceiling effects that mask pipeline differences. The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 passed all initial candidates in this run; future work should validate and quantify validator sensitivity.

Task set external validity: tasks were synthetic, deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 items with redaction rules per the preregistration; results may not generalize to heterogeneous production configurations or vendor quirks.
Single model and adapter: only gpt-5-mini and one adapter instance were used; results do not establish model‑class generality.

Sampling record: temperature=null/unset in archived model configuration does not imply deterministic sampling; independent per‑condition sampling would be required to evaluate generation‑level effects.
